elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose third-party commercial offers to Vendor for MFN purposes.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer has no obligation to disclose any commercial offer it receives.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match third-party offers or otherwise provide Vendor with most-favoured-customer terms.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly disclaims both matching obligations and any obligation to give Vendor most-favoured-customer terms; Section 12.3 independently confirms that no most-favoured-customer commitment has been made.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it applies only to an expressly defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered language eliminates any MFN obligation burdening Customer, so no broader product scope remains.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, its duration is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Customer has no MFN obligation under the rendered language, including no obligation extending beyond 12 months.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it applies only to reasonably comparable offers or transactions and excludes non-comparable circumstances.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered language eliminates the MFN obligation entirely, so Customer cannot be required to compare or match non-comparable offers.

result.reason: The redline directly removes the disclose-and-match obligation and expressly confirms that Customer owes no most-favoured-customer terms. It therefore achieves the preferred position; the fallback limitations are also satisfied because their predicate—an MFN obligation burdening Customer—is demonstrably absent. Section 12.3 remains effective and consistent. The statement that MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome is permissive rather than a required operative term.
